page: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal instance within the compute-optimized family, providing direct hardware access without virtualization overhead. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor based on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 36 physical cores and 72 execution threads at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 192 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, providing approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 vector extensions alongside standard cryptographic instructions. The instance incorporates a high-speed 100 Gbps network interface, but contains no local storage and does not bundle dedicated GPUs.

Synthetic benchmark results reflect the high degree of CPU parallelism and memory capability. In multi-threaded evaluation, c5n.metal registers 67,384.33 on stress-ng and 50,868.09 on the PassMark CPU suite, ranking in the upper quartile of tested instances. Memory throughput reaches 212.97 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 3,741.32 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read operations. Application benchmarks show strong performance in code compilation, achieving a score of 39,606.0 in Clang tests, as well as 22,478.14 in PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,193.0 and stress-ng single-core result of 1,458.4, occupy mid-range percentiles. Autoregressive language model generation is similarly constrained, measuring 6.09 tokens per second on a 7B model.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, c5n.metal delivers substantial compute density and network bandwidth per instance, eliminating hypervisor contention for predictable execution. The primary operational tradeoff stems from the complete absence of local non-volatile storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage architectures that leverage the 100 Gbps network link. This configuration aligns with distributed compute grids, large-scale software compilation farms, network traffic processing appliances, and scale-out relational or in-memory databases that benefit from dedicated physical resources.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.metal is a bare-metal compute-optimized server engineered for high-throughput, network-intensive computational tasks. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz across 36 physical cores and 72 execution threads, it includes AVX-512 extensions and 192 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. The platform features 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating large data flows, though it includes no onboard local storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-threaded performance in PassMark CPU tests, high multi-core stress-ng throughput, and fast software compilation via Clang, complemented by substantial cached and uncached memory bandwidth. In contrast, single-core metrics and LLM token generation rates remain modest. The c5n.metal instance is particularly matched for network appliances, distributed analytics, clustered scientific computation, code compilation, and database workloads requiring dedicated bare-metal hardware access without hypervisor overhead.
